raw_response:
I farm in Quzhou County, Hebei, where the common and safest pattern for me is the winter wheat and summer maize rotation. I would keep doing that this year because it fits my land, my experience, the local water conditions, and the machinery I can manage. At the start of the growing season, I would first focus on the winter wheat already in the field, then I would prepare for summer maize right after wheat harvest so I do not lose time. I would use improved seed for wheat because it is steadier and easier for me to manage, and hybrid seed for maize because I care most about stable yield. I would not spread my land into many different crops, because with my age, education, and labor limits, I would rather run one familiar rotation well than take risks on complicated cash crops. For wheat, I would use moderate fertilizer, irrigate a few times at key stages, and spray only when needed for disease, aphids, or weeds. After harvest, I would sow maize quickly, use more nitrogen than wheat, irrigate in the key summer periods depending on rain, and control weeds and insects with a few planned pesticide applications. I would use rotary tillage for wheat and no-tillage direct seeding for maize after wheat if conditions allow, because that saves time and helps me catch the season.
